title: Smooth ball bumps in finite-dimensional real inner product spaces
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, $c\in E$ and $0<a<b$. There exists a smooth real function $\rho:E\to\mathbf R$, with $0\leq\rho\leq1$, equal to $1$ on $\{x:\|x-c\|\leq a\}$, such that the closure of $\{x:\rho(x)\neq0\}$ is the compact closed ball $\{x:\|x-c\|\leq b\}$. Smooth means infinitely differentiable over $\mathbf R$.
